g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=4) State-space models (Gu et al., 2021; Hasani et al., 2022; Smith et al., 2023; Orvieto et al., 2023) have recently emerged as a powerful tool for learning on long sequences.

g.text: These models posses the statefullness and fast inference capabilities of
Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) together with many of the benefits of
Transformers (Vaswani, 2017; Devlin, 2018), such as efficient training and
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=2) These models posses the statefullness and fast inference capabilities of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) together with many of the benefits of Transformers (Vaswani, 2017; Devlin, 2018), such as efficient training and competitive performance on large-scale language and image modeling tasks.

g.text: For these reasons, state-space models have been successfully implemented as
foundation models, surpassing Transformer-based counterparts in several key
modalities, including language, audio, and genomics (Gu & Dao, 2023).
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=1) For these reasons, state-space models have been successfully implemented as foundation models, surpassing Transformer-based counterparts in several key modalities, including language, audio, and genomics (Gu & Dao, 2023).

g.text: Originally, state-space models have been introduced to modern sequence
modelling by leveraging specific structures of the state matrix, i.e.,
normal plus low-rank HiPPO matrices (Gu et al., 2020; 2021), allowing to
g.title: N4 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) Originally, state-space models have been introduced to modern sequence modelling by leveraging specific structures of the state matrix, i.e., normal plus low-rank HiPPO matrices (Gu et al., 2020; 2021), allowing to solve linear recurrences via a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT).

g.text: This has since been simplified to only requiring diagonal state matrices (Gu
et al., 2022a; Smith et al., 2023; Orvieto et al., 2023) while still
obtaining similar or even better performance.
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=3) This has since been simplified to only requiring diagonal state matrices (Gu et al., 2022a; Smith et al., 2023; Orvieto et al., 2023) while still obtaining similar or even better performance.

g.text: However, due to the linear nature of state-space models, the corresponding
state matrices need to fulfill specific structural properties in order to
learn long-range interactions and produce stable predictions.
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, due to the linear nature of state-space models, the corresponding state matrices need to fulfill specific structural properties in order to learn long-range interactions and produce stable predictions.

g.text: Consequently, these structural requirements heavily constrain the underlying
latent feature space, potentially impairing the model's expressive power.
g.title: N7 [Limitation] (cites=0) Consequently, these structural requirements heavily constrain the underlying latent feature space, potentially impairing the model's expressive power.

g.title: N8 [Method] (cites=0) In this article, we adopt a radically different approach by observing that forced harmonic oscillators, the basis of many systems in physics, biology, and engineering, can produce stable dynamics while at the same time seem to ensure expressive representations.

g.text: Motivated by this, we propose to construct state-space models based on
stable discretizations of forced linear second-order ordinary differential
g.title: N9 [Method] (cites=0) Motivated by this, we propose to construct state-space models based on stable discretizations of forced linear second-order ordinary differential equations (ODEs) modelling oscillators.
C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) we introduce implicit and implicit-explicit associative parallel scans ensuring fast training and inference.

g.text: we show that our proposed state-space model
yields stable dynamics and is able to learn
g.title: C2 [Contribution] (cites=0) we show that our proposed state-space model yields stable dynamics and is able to learn long-range interactions only requiring nonnegative diagonal state matrix.
C3 [Contribution] (cites=0) we demonstrate that a symplectic discretization of our underlying oscillatory system conserves its symmetry of time reversibility.

g.title: C4 [Contribution] (cites=0) we rigorously prove that our proposed state-space model is a universal approximator of continuous and causal operators between time-series.

g.title: C5 [Contribution] (cites=0) we provide an extensive empirical evaluation of our model on a wide variety of sequential data sets with sequence lengths reaching up to 50k. Our results demonstrate that our model consistently outperforms or matches the performance of state-of-the-art state-space models, including Mamba, S4, S5, and LRU.
